## Historical audit — S0133

**Scope:** Only chunk 3 is visible. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Character ranges identify the supplied observations, not independently inspected images.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 19 [0,289482), student request and embedded build history | The stated goal was to reconstruct a 512 × 388 indoor photograph with separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, occlusion and color. The student interpreted it as an electronics workbench; this semantic interpretation is not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Line 19 [0,289482), student step 1 program | The program constructs multiple assemblies: bench and walls, monitor, oscilloscope, meters, keyboard, lamp, cabinets, tools and foreground clutter. It specifies solid panels, separate components, colored materials, a noise/bump attempt for the desktop, camera, world and area lights. Grouping and coordinates indicate intended support and connections, but do not verify physical contact or completeness. The meter and keyboard are rotated; the monitor is turned. |
| Line 19 [0,289482), step 1 feedback and step 2 program | The runner reports `ok: true` and a render available. The student estimated the monitor was too short and insufficiently oblique, then enlarged, rotated and shifted its display while adjusting its stand. This was a local geometry/pose correction, not a camera change. The claimed landmark discrepancies and preservation regions are student visual estimates. |
| Line 19 [0,289482), step 2 feedback and step 3 program | Step 2 also reports a render available. The student claimed its monitor silhouette improved but the desktop and drawer fronts were too pale, and changed their color parameters while retaining camera and lighting. Step 3 reports `ok: true` and a render available. Texture application, tone improvement, framing and occlusion are not independently verified by those reports. |
| Lines 20 [0,4267), 21 [0,342), 22 [0,59) | A fresh read-only student session received references to the photograph and three renders, had no tool calls, and returned `SELECT 3`; the subsequent selection event records step 3. |

**Input and exploration.** The visible input includes system and runner instructions to compare actual renders, prioritize broad structure and choose a coherent correction. The student’s two successive diagnoses and revisions are visible autonomous exploration within that prescribed procedure. No distinct teacher message, teacher detection or diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or evidence of teacher-feedback adoption appears in this chunk; availability elsewhere would not establish receipt.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Three builds formally executed successfully and step 3 was selected; this is **execution success, with reconstruction correctness unknown**, not independent visual or geometric validation. The images themselves are not visible in this audit. Whether the monitor remains connected to its stand, whether the procedural texture actually affected the desktop, and whether camera, lighting, object coverage or final tones match the reference remain unresolved hypotheses. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is shown here.

**Lessons.** Transferable process evidence is the separation of a local silhouette revision from a later regional color revision, each followed by a reported render. The particular monitor scaling and darkening values are task-specific hypotheses, not verified improvements.
